_meta.what_this_is: Anscombe's quartet: four small (x,y) datasets constructed by Francis Anscombe in 1973 to have NEARLY IDENTICAL summary statistics -- same mean of x, mean of y, variance, correlation, and least-squares regression line -- while looking completely different when plotted. d1 is a clean linear relationship; d2 is a perfect curve (a parabola); d3 is linear with one extreme outlier; d4 is a vertical line of points at x=8 plus one far-out point that alone creates the correlation. The point: the summary stats agree to two decimals and the datasets could not be more different, so a number is never a substitute for looking at the data.
_meta.data_is: The actual Anscombe (1973) quartet -- a canonical published dataset, reproduced here so the identical statistics and the differing shapes are exact and checkable.
